criteria.criterion: Athena's verdict code (crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, fed by crates/athena-core/src/run.rs) compares docs/design/requirements-map.md at the base with the candidate. For every row whose status changed to Covered from Partial or Not covered, or that was added already Covered, it adds an Athena-sourced major finding naming the row ID. So the final verdict cannot be pass. Rows that stay Covered, or move away from Covered, add no finding.
criteria.evidence: In verify.rs, rows_newly_covered() returns each row that is Covered at the candidate and was not Covered at the base. judge() turns each one into athena_finding(Severity::Major, ...) with the row ID in the summary, plus a reason. Its row parser uses the same rule as the CLI's parse_map (strategy.rs lines 61-84). In run.rs, map_base and map_candidate are read with vsnap.git().show_file("HEAD~1"/"HEAD", MAP_PATH). show_file returns None when the file is absent (athena-git lib.rs:386).

summary: The change closes both gaps the request names. The verifier prompt now tells the verifier to read any document a request cites and compare the change with it, and says falling short is a request_reading_mismatch. This rule is prose-only, and docs/enforcement.md records that. In code, judge() compares docs/design/requirements-map.md at the base with the candidate. For each row that became Covered, it adds a major finding that names the row and is raised by Athena itself, so the verifier cannot leave it out; that makes the verdict fail. The run.rs code reads the map from the verifier's snapshot at HEAD~1 and HEAD. The producer prompt states the rule. A9-1 and A10-1 are back to Partial, each with its reason. The G5 counts and lists in the strategy view match the map. The decision entry D94, the changelog, enforcement row M32 and the roles-and-ladder note are all updated. I ran the verify unit tests, the budgets test, the whole workspace test suite, clippy and fmt in this snapshot, and all passed. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. One minor gap: no test covers the run.rs code that reads the map, so only judge() itself is tested.
